reuse.why: Builds the change into the existing shared applyWeekendRule and only threads frequency through parseRecurDate so the rule data reaches it.

duplication.why: The daily-skip rule is written once; callers only adapt to the new nullable result, and the schedule-template loop is simplified rather than copied.

placement.why: The weekend rule stays in shared/schedules.ts where the tree defines it; server callers keep their iteration logic.

scope.why: Touches only the rule, the data it needs, the three callers that must handle a skipped occurrence, tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: Clear single rule with a nullable contract; the 'look 7 occurrences ahead' bound is repeated as a magic number in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every weekend-handling path (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, schedule-template createScheduleList) still goes through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; the over-fetch bound appears twice but is a constant, not a rule copy.

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts applyWeekendRule decides skip-vs-move for daily schedules; getNextDate, schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and budget/schedule-template.ts all call it.
